title: Plan entitlements, quota windows and overage billing PRD for usage-based plans
creator: Asha Menon
description: PRD defining plan entitlements, quota window semantics, enforcement modes (soft vs hard), and overage billing rules for Redwood hosted usage-based plans. Goal: create a single source of truth for product, billing, and engineering teams so that plan behavior is predictable and billable events are auditable.
background: Customer feedback and internal audits revealed ambiguity in how quotas reset, how short windows (rate limits) interact with monthly quotas, and when overage charges are applied. Existing behavior was inconsistent across hosted and dedicated plans. This PRD unifies semantics and specifies acceptance criteria for billing integration, API responses, console UX, and migration behavior.
requirements: Define entitlement model: per-plan limits (tokens, embeddings units, concurrent requests) with optional add-on SKUs
Quota windows: support rolling 30-day, calendar-month, and custom subscription-aligned windows; document rollover behavior
Rate limits: configurable per-second and per-minute tiers; support burst allowance and token-based weightings
Enforcement modes: soft (warning + throttling suggestion) and hard (reject with 429); default policy per plan with per-customer overrides
Overage billing: automated invoice line items generated daily for overage usage, with configurable grace thresholds and caps
Billing primitives: usage events must be idempotent, timestamped, include request metadata, and exportable via webhook and console
Migration: existing customers must be migrated with no unexpected charges; provide a preview tool and opt-in transition window
Console & API UX: expose remaining quotas, forecasted overage estimates, and rate-limit headers in API responses
Testing & telemetry: unit and e2e tests for quota enforcement, and dashboards for accuracy, latency, and billing reconciliation
scope: Implement plan entitlement model across hosted API and Console; add backend billing pipeline hooks for daily overage aggregation; update API responses to include quota headers; provide migration preview for existing customers.
out_of_scope: Dedicated and Private on-prem billing connectors (handled in separate initiative)
Complex chargeback features for internal platform teams
acceptance_criteria: Entitlement config UI allows product to create/update plan limits and add-on SKUs with audit trail
Quota windows implemented: rolling-30d and calendar-month produce identical results to spec for 95% of synthetic test traces
API returns X-Remaining-Quota, X-Quota-Reset and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers for all rate-limited endpoints
Soft enforcement mode issues warnings in console and emits 'quota.warning' webhook events but does not charge overage unless soft threshold is crossed twice in 7 days
Hard enforcement returns 429 with descriptive error code and documentation link; logs contain customer id, plan id, and reason
Daily overage aggregation pipeline produces invoice-ready line items with idempotency keys and passes reconciliation tests against billing ledger
Migration preview tool shows per-customer projected charges for 3 months and must be signed-off by Finance before opt-in is enabled
At least three load-tested scenarios (steady, bursty, and long-tail) validate correctness and latency impact under 99th percentile SLOs
End-to-end billing accuracy within 0.1% compared to ground-truth in the reconciliation sandbox for test customers
implementation_notes: Use existing usage-event schema but add 'quota_window' and 'entitlement_snapshot' fields for reconciliation (store as strings referencing snapshot ids)
Leverage billing-queue (ENG-2014) for daily aggregation; ensure consumer is idempotent and supports at-least-once semantics
Rate-limit enforcement should read from a cached entitlement store (TTL 60s) and fall back to DB for cold starts
Console exposure: add a per-customer quota panel and forecast widget that samples recent 7/30-day consumption
Legal: include grace and overage terms in TOS; coordinate with Legal for messaging templates
